summary_zh: 总统似乎让万斯和卢比奥作为潜在的继任者进行了测试，尽管斯蒂芬·米勒出人意料地抢走了风头。
body_en: The president appeared to put Vance and Rubio through their paces as potential successors, though Stephen Miller unexpectedly stole the spotlight
“Which of you shall we say doth love us most?”
The ageing King Lear’s question to his daughters, expecting them to compete for his favour and carve up his kingdom, hovered in the White House press briefing room on Friday.

There at the lectern stood Donald “Lear” Trump. Behind him stood his potential heirs, JD “Goneril” Vance and Marco “Regan” Rubio, and to the side sat Trump’s favourite offspring, Stephen “Cordelia” Miller (more of him later). As for Lear’s Fool, the choices were endless.

Ostensibly this was a press conference to trumpet the president’s trip in Asia, but in practice everyone knew it was the first audition for the 2028 presidential election (and boy, is Trump going to enjoy turning the race into a contest for his approval). Vance is widely expected to seek the crown, though it was Rubio who came out on top in the latest Emerson College national poll .

In a jam-packed room, Trump stood centre stage as if hosting The Apprentice all over again. Behind him were the two contenders expressing their aspirations through matching suits, matching Maga red ties, matching US flag pins and matching leather shoes.

The first trial: could Vance and Rubio stand still for 90 minutes without rolling their eyes, yawning or silently mouthing “Kill me!” to the press? Could they force Trump’s word salad down their throats and look as if they were enjoying it? Even when the boss was rambling at length about potholes?

“When you fix a pothole”, began one detour by the octogenarian president. “I don’t want to bore you – they’ll say, oh, he rambled, he rambled terribly. I don’t ramble. I don’t ramble at all, but when you fix a pothole, you have brand new asphalt against old white asphalt that doesn’t look good, but at least you don’t ruin your car, but these roads were flawless …”

But first, the whole thing got off to a strange start. Trump appeared at the podium and remarked: “That’s a big, big a crowd. I’ve never seen this before,” but reporters crammed in the room could barely hear him above the whoosh of an air conditioning unit. An engineer tweaked the sound, but it only gave Trump’s voice an eerie echo.

Had the gremlins that grounded flights and frozen banking sites finally reached the White House? So much for America the hi-tech superpower. Eventually order was restored, though not necessarily in Trump’s brain.

He was evidently flattered by the media comparing his trilateral summit with the leaders of China and Russia to the Yalta meeting between Winston Churchill, Franklin Roosevelt and Joseph Stalin (he did not say which of the three he identified with, though critics could take a guess). Like a gushing teenager, Trump was so thrilled that Chinese president Xi Jinping had come to the airport to greet him, that he mentioned it twice (“He didn’t meet Sleepy Joe with the plane, that I can tell you.”)

The US, Russia and China hold 92% of global nuclear power, he noted, which gave him an excuse to bring up his uncle John Trump , an electrical engineer and former Massachusetts Institute of Technology professor. “A member of my family spent his life at MIT who they say is now the greatest professor in the history of MIT, so I have great understanding of- I guess maybe genetically I’m blessed,” Trump riffed.

At that remark Rubio could resist no longer. A smile spread across his lips and he shot a look at Vance, who felt obliged to smile back. We’re not laughing at you, we’re laughing with you, Mr President.

Indeed, Rubio had been the more fidgety of the pair. As Trump chuntered on, the secretary of state had shifted from foot to foot, fiddled with his tie, played with his lower lip, touched up his hair and given the odd wry smile. Vance, meanwhile, hid behind his beard and miasma of smugness.

But then, at last, came the moment for Lear’s daughters to make their public declarations of love. Vance went up the lectern and pointed out that he had stayed in Washington rather than joining the trip, comparing himself to Macaulay Culkin’s character in Home Alone – a child who is accidentally left behind at Christmas as his family rushes to catch a flight to Paris. “I missed you, sir,” he said to Trump, before praising the president for “securing historic trade deals” and reorganising the global economy to benefit the American worker and economy.

Not bad, but a little wonky. Marco, you’re up next. The secretary of state took aim at the critics who accused Trump of cosying up to dictators at the expense of Democrats, raising his eyebrows and shaking his fist: “These three countries possess the overwhelming majority of nuclear weapons on this planet. The idea that these three leaders should not engage on a regular basis is not just absurd, it’s dangerous.”

Trump began taking reporters’ questions. One young whippersnapper posed a question that will be asked many times over the next two years. “Because you have the vice-president, the secretary of state right behind you, I’m curious which of them do you think would make a better president after you?”
Trump swatted it aside without answering. Vance remained stony faced. Rubio smiled knowingly.

The same reporter put Vance in an uncomfortable spot by asking about his post-midterm tweet. “Would you argue that the war in Iran was worth it to lose the Senate?” The vice-president agreed with the goal of Iran not getting a nuclear weapon but added carefully: “I think the president is the one who makes the decision and the president has said he would do it again. And my view is that my goal is and my job is to support the president of the United States.”
body_zh: 总统似乎让万斯和卢比奥作为潜在的继任者，尽管斯蒂芬·米勒出人意料地抢走了风头
“我们该说你们谁最爱我们呢？”
周五，白宫新闻发布厅里一直萦绕着年迈的李尔王向女儿们提出的问题，希望她们能争夺他的青睐并瓜分他的王国。
讲台上站着唐纳德·“李尔”·特朗普。在他身后站着他的潜在继承人 JD “Goneril” Vance 和 Marco “Regan” Rubio，旁边坐着特朗普最喜欢的后代 Stephen “Cordelia” Miller（稍后会详细介绍）。至于李尔的愚人，选择是无穷无尽的。
表面上这是一场宣传总统亚洲之行的新闻发布会，但实际上每个人都知道这是 2028 年总统选举的第一次试镜（天哪，特朗普会喜欢把竞选变成一场争取他认可的竞赛吗）。人们普遍预计万斯将争夺桂冠，尽管卢比奥在艾默生学院最新的全国民意调查中名列前茅。
在拥挤的房间里，特朗普站在舞台中央，仿佛再次招待了《学徒》。在他身后，两位参赛者通过相配的西装、相配的马加红色领带、相配的美国国旗别针和相配的皮鞋表达了自己的愿望。
第一个考验：万斯和卢比奥能否在90分钟内保持不动，不翻白眼、不打哈欠、不默念“杀了我！”向媒体？他们能否强行将特朗普的话语强行咽下，并表现出一副很享受的样子？即使老板滔滔不绝地谈论坑洼？
“当你修复坑洼时”，这位八十多岁的总统开始绕道而行。 “我不想让你厌烦——他们会说，哦，他胡言乱语，他胡言乱语得很厉害。我不胡言乱语。我根本不胡言乱语，但是当你修复一个坑洼时，你会得到全新的沥青和旧的白色沥青，看起来不太好，但至少你不会毁掉你的车，但这些道路是完美的……”
但首先，整件事有一个奇怪的开始。特朗普出现在讲台上并说道：“这是一大群人。我以前从未见过这样的情况。”但挤在房间里的记者在空调的呼啸声中几乎听不到他的声音。一名工程师调整了声音，但这只给特朗普的声音带来了怪异的回声。
那些导致航班停飞和银行网站冻结的小恶魔终于抵达白宫了吗？美国这个高科技超级大国就到此为止了。最终秩序得到了恢复，尽管不一定是在特朗普的大脑中。
媒体将他与中国和俄罗斯领导人的三边峰会与温斯顿·丘吉尔、富兰克林·罗斯福和约瑟夫·斯大林之间的雅尔塔会晤进行比较（他没有说出他认同三者中的哪一个，尽管批评者可以猜测），这显然让他感到受宠若惊。就像一个滔滔不绝的青少年一样，特朗普对中国国家主席习近平来到机场迎接他感到非常兴奋，他两次提到了这一点（“我可以告诉你，他没有在飞机上遇见瞌睡乔。”）
他指出，美国、俄罗斯和中国拥有全球 92% 的核电，这给了他一个借口来提拔他的叔叔约翰·特朗普 (John Trump)，后者是一名电气工程师、前麻省理工学院教授。 “我的一位家人在麻省理工学院度过了一生，他们说他现在是麻省理工学院历史上最伟大的教授，所以我对此非常了解——我想也许从基因上来说我很幸运，”特朗普反复说道。
听到这句话，卢比奥再也无法抗拒。他的嘴角绽开一丝微笑，他看了万斯一眼，万斯也不得不回以微笑。总统先生，我们不是在笑你，而是和你一起笑。
事实上，卢比奥是两人中最烦躁的一个。当特朗普喋喋不休时，国务卿不断变换着姿势，摆弄着领带，玩弄着下唇，抚摸着头发，露出奇怪的苦笑。与此同时，万斯躲在他的胡子和沾沾自喜的瘴气后面。
但最后，李尔王的女儿们公开示爱的时刻到来了。万斯走上讲台，指出他留在华盛顿而不是参加这次旅行，并将自己与麦考利卡尔金在《小鬼当家》中的角色进行了比较——一个在圣诞节期间因家人急于飞往巴黎而意外被留在家里的孩子。 “我想念你，先生，”他对特朗普说道，然后赞扬总统“确保了历史性贸易协议”并重组了全球经济，使美国工人和经济受益。
不错，但有点不稳定。马可，下一个是你。国务卿针对那些指责特朗普以牺牲民主党为代价来讨好独裁者的批评者，他扬起眉毛，挥舞着拳头：“这三个国家拥有这个星球上绝大多数的核武器。认为这三位领导人不应该定期接触的想法不仅荒谬，而且很危险。”
特朗普开始回答记者提问。一位年轻的自吹自擂者提出了一个在未来两年内将被多次问到的问题。 “因为你身后有副总统、国务卿，我很好奇你认为他们中谁会在你之后成为更好的总统？”
特朗普把它扔到一边，没有回答。万斯面无表情。卢比奥会心一笑。
这位记者询问了万斯中期选举后的推文，这让他陷入了尴尬的境地。 “你认为伊朗战争值得失去参议院吗？”副总统同意伊朗不获得核武器的目标，但谨慎地补充道：“我认为总统是做出决定的人，总统已经说过他会再做一次。我的观点是，我的目标和我的工作是支持美国总统。”

body_en: Senator Thom Tillis , a North Carolina Republican who is about to be replaced by a Democrat, told multiple news outlets that he has blocked a confirmation vote on Donald Trump ’s nominee to lead the federal government’s cybersecurity and infrastructure security agency (Cisa), Michael LoSapio , one day after the nominee denied that the US Capitol was attacked on January 6 2021.

Tillis, who elected not to run for re-election without Trump’s support, confirmed to HuffPost on Friday that he has placed a hold on LoSapio’s nomination, which will prevent it from being included in a package of nominees to be voted on next month, before the Republicans lose their majority in the Senate.
Tillis previously told a reporter for Punchbowl on Thursday that he would use the procedural move to delay a vote on LoSapio’s confirmation before Democrats take power in January.

At his Senate confirmation hearing on Thursday, LoSapio, the chief information security officer for Palantir, a technology firm founded by JD Vance’s mentor, Peter Thiel, was asked by senator Richard Blumenthal , a Connecticut Democrat, “Was there an attack on the Capitol of January 6 2021?”
After initially replying, “I don’t know,” LoSapio said, “No, I don’t believe it was an attack.”
The agency LoSapio was nominated by Trump to lead, Cisa, plays a role in protecting US elections infrastructure from hacking.

The week after the 2020 election, as Trump falsely claimed that count had been rigged, Cisa was one of a number of federal agencies with oversight of election infrastructure to issue a statement calling the election “the most secure in American history” and noting that there was “no evidence that any voting system deleted or lost votes, changed votes, or was in any way compromised.”

After he returned to the White House last year, Trump signed an April 2025 presidential memorandum directing executive offices to take steps to address supposed “risks from Chris Krebs,” who lead Cisa in 2020. “Krebs, through CISA, falsely and baselessly denied that the 2020 election was rigged and stolen, including by inappropriately and categorically dismissing widespread election malfeasance and serious vulnerabilities with voting machines,” Trump’s memorandum claimed.
body_zh: 即将被民主党接替的北卡罗来纳州共和党参议员汤姆·蒂利斯 (Thom Tillis) 向多家新闻媒体表示，他已阻止对唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 提名的联邦政府网络安全和基础设施安全机构 (Cisa) 负责人迈克尔·洛萨皮奥 (Michael LoSapio) 进行确认投票，而一天前，该提名人否认美国国会大厦于 2021 年 1 月 6 日遭到袭击。
蒂利斯选择在没有特朗普支持的情况下不再竞选连任，他周五向《赫芬顿邮报》证实，他已暂停洛萨皮奥的提名，这将阻止其被纳入下个月在共和党失去参议院多数席位之前投票的一揽子提名人。
蒂利斯此前于周四对 Punchbowl 的记者表示，他将利用这一程序举措，在民主党一月份掌权之前推迟对 LoSapio 的确认投票。
在周四的参议院确认听证会上，JD Vance 的导师 Peter Thiel 创立的科技公司 Palantir 的首席信息安全官 LoSapio 被康涅狄格州民主党参议员理查德·布卢门撒尔问到：“2021 年 1 月 6 日国会大厦是否发生过袭击？”
洛萨皮奥最初回答说“我不知道”，“不，我不相信这是一次攻击”。
由特朗普提名领导的机构 LoSapio Cisa 在保护美国选举基础设施免遭黑客攻击方面发挥着作用。
2020 年大选结束后一周，特朗普错误地声称计票被操纵，CISA 是众多负责监督选举基础设施的联邦机构之一，他们发表声明称这次选举是“美国历史上最安全的一次”，并指出“没有证据表明任何投票系统删除或丢失选票、更改选票或以任何方式受到损害”。
去年回到白宫后，特朗普签署了 2025 年 4 月的总统备忘录，指示行政办公室采取措施，解决所谓的“来自 2020 年领导 CISA 的克里斯·克雷布斯 (Chris Krebs) 的风险”。“克雷布斯通过 CISA 错误地、毫无根据地否认 2020 年选举被操纵和窃取，包括不恰当地、明确地否认普遍存在的选举舞弊行为和投票机的严重漏洞。”备忘录声称。

body_en: Republican senator blocks Trump cyber nominee over January 6 denial | Republicans
Thom Tillis move comes after Michael LoSapio, nominated for Cisa role, told hearing ‘I don’t believe it was an attack’

Senator Thom Tillis, the outgoing North Carolina Republican who is due to be replaced by a Democrat, has reportedly blocked a confirmation vote on Donald Trump’s nominee to lead a key US cybersecurity agency, Michael LoSapio, after he denied during a hearing that the Capitol was attacked on January 6 2021.

Tillis, who declined to run for re-election and after repeated clashes with Trump’s, confirmed to HuffPost on Friday that he has placed a hold on LoSapio’s nomination to serve as a director of the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Agency (Cisa). His block on the nomination will prevent it from being included in a package of nominees to be voted on next month, before the Republicans lose their majority in the Senate.

At his Senate confirmation hearing on Thursday, LoSapio, the chief information security officer for Palantir, a technology firm founded by JD Vance’s mentor, Peter Thiel, was asked by senator Richard Blumenthal, a Connecticut Democrat: “Was there an attack on the Capitol of January 6 2021?”
After initially replying, “I don’t know,” LoSapio said: “No, I don’t believe it was an attack.”
Tillis told the Hill that the question of whether a mob of Trump supporters attacked the US Capitol in an attempt to overturn Joe Biden’s 2020 victory was not open for debate.
“It’s binary,” Tillis told the outlet. “The minute you pretend like it didn’t exist or you can’t even acknowledge it, I don’t have any time because it’s not a very thoughtful person.”
The agency LoSapio was nominated by Trump to lead, Cisa, plays a role in protecting US elections infrastructure from hacking.

The week after the 2020 election, as Trump falsely claimed that count had been rigged, Cisa was one of a number of federal agencies with oversight of election infrastructure to issue a statement calling the election “the most secure in American history” and noting that there was “no evidence that any voting system deleted or lost votes, changed votes, or was in any way compromised.”

After he returned to the White House last year, Trump signed an April 2025 presidential memorandum directing executive offices to take steps to address supposed “risks from Chris Krebs”, who led Cisa in 2020.

“Krebs, through CISA, falsely and baselessly denied that the 2020 election was rigged and stolen, including by inappropriately and categorically dismissing widespread election malfeasance and serious vulnerabilities with voting machines,” Trump’s memorandum claimed.

2020 年大选结束后一周，特朗普错误地声称计票被操纵，CISA 是众多负责监督选举基础设施的联邦机构之一，他们发表声明称这次选举是“美国历史上最安全的一次”，并指出“没有证据表明任何投票系统删除或丢失选票、更改选票或以任何方式受到损害”。
去年重返白宫后，特朗普于 2025 年 4 月签署了一份总统备忘录，指示行政办公室采取措施应对所谓的“来自 2020 年领导 CISA 的克里斯·克雷布斯 (Chris Krebs) 的风险”。

body_en: Trump threatens ‘tremendous penalties’ for US tech firms that build datacenters abroad | Donald Trump
President gives wide-ranging White House press conference and says he has ‘fantastic relationships’ with Putin and Xi

Donald Trump threatened on Friday to impose “tremendous penalties” on American tech companies that build datacenters outside the US, though he gave no details and told reporters he had not yet informed his own officials about the plan.

In a discursive press conference from the White House briefing room, Trump also said he would “look into” the report that Iran had been planning to possibly detonate a “dirty bomb” in Washington DC, and backed JD Vance over comments the vice-president made blaming Republican midterm losses on the Iran war.

Trump also expounded on his friendship with the Russian president Vladimir Putin, whom he met alongside China’s Xi Jinping at the Apec summit on Thursday, adding he had “fantastic relationships” with both autocratic leaders.
At the White House, Trump told reporters he wanted datacenters built by US companies to stay on US soil.

“We’re not allowing datacenters to go into other countries, because China will take all of them, and we’re not allowing that to happen. And we’re going to put tremendous penalties on companies that try to do it,” he said.
He said Americans should welcome datacenters, and urged communities to extract concessions from developers, repeating a point he made before the midterms.
“You ought to take advantage of the datacenters. Make them pay you, make them pay your community, but don’t shut them off,” he said.

With many Americans turning against the datacenters being built near their homes, the US tech industry is making a show of conciliation by promising to take fewer government handouts, to be more transparent, and to give more money to towns and cities willing to allow server warehouses to be built.

The Trump administration on Monday issued new rules to restrict remote access to advanced US computing chips and servers, in a move it said was designed to limit China’s ability to use US chips to train its artificial intelligence models – though a House committee said on Wednesday the US had signed off on sales of nearly 900,000 AI chips to China in six months.

China’s ability to obtain advanced AI chips made by the US firm Nvidia, in which Trump is an investor, has been spotlighted in recent weeks after its CEO, Jensen Huang, was fired over his affair with a woman alleged to be spying for China.

In the same press conference, Trump was asked about reports Iran was planning to potentially detonate an explosive laced with nuclear material – a so-called “dirty bomb” – in Washington DC. The president called it a “rumour” and said: “If they do, we’re going to fight.”
He added: “We know a lot about what’s happening in Iran. We know everything they say. We know who they are, where they are. We’ll find out about it.”
Responding to a question about reports of a rift with Vance, Trump said the vice-president’s remark blaming the Republican collapse on the Iran war was “a very accurate statement”.

“I didn’t say I was unhappy with it,” the president said. “I would have added one other thing if it were asked … would you do it again? And absolutely, the answer is yes, because we cannot allow Iran to have a nuclear weapon.”
Trump was asked whether Vladimir Putin could really be considered a friend to America since Russia is a close ally of Iran.

“I can’t speak to America,” he said, adding: “I consider [that] I have fantastic relationships with Putin. That’s a very good thing. I have fantastic relationships with President Xi. That’s a good thing, and our country is safe because of that.”
He praised Putin as he repeated his grievances over the Department of Justice’s investigation into the Russian attempts to influence US voters ahead of the 2016 presidential election.
body_zh: 特朗普威胁对在海外建设数据中心的美国科技公司实施“巨额处罚”唐纳德·特朗普
总统在白宫举行了内容广泛的新闻发布会，并表示他与普京和习近平有着“极好的关系”
唐纳德·特朗普周五威胁要对在美国境外建立数据中心的美国科技公司实施“巨额处罚”，但他没有透露细节，并告诉记者，他尚未将该计划告知本国官员。
在白宫新闻发布会上，特朗普还表示，他将“调查”伊朗计划在华盛顿特区引爆“脏弹”的报道，并支持副总统万斯将共和党中期选举失败归咎于伊朗战争的言论。
特朗普还阐述了他与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京的友谊，他在周四的亚太经合组织峰会上与中国国家主席习近平会面，并补充说他与两位独裁领导人有着“极好的关系”。
特朗普在白宫告诉记者，他希望美国公司建造的数据中心留在美国领土上。
“我们不允许数据中心进入其他国家，因为中国将把它们全部拿走，我们不会允许这种情况发生。我们将对试图这样做的公司处以巨额处罚，”他说。
他表示美国人应该欢迎数据中心，并敦促社区从开发商那里获得让步，重复了他在中期选举前提出的观点。
“你应该利用数据中心。让他们付钱给你，让他们付钱给你的社区，但不要关闭它们，”他说。
随着许多美国人反对在他们家附近建造数据中心，美国科技行业正在做出和解的姿态，承诺减少政府的施舍，提高透明度，并向愿意允许建造服务器仓库的城镇提供更多资金。
特朗普政府周一发布了新规则，限制远程访问美国先进计算芯片和服务器，据称此举旨在限制中国使用美国芯片训练其人工智能模型的能力，尽管众议院委员会周三表示，美国已批准在六个月内向中国出售近 90 万个人工智能芯片。
最近几周，在特朗普投资的美国公司英伟达 (Nvidia) 首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 因与一名涉嫌为中国从事间谍活动的女性有染而被解雇后，中国获得特朗普投资的英伟达 (Nvidia) 制造的先进人工智能芯片的能力受到关注。
在同一次新闻发布会上，特朗普被问及有关伊朗计划在华盛顿特区引爆含有核材料的爆炸物（所谓的“脏弹”）的报道。总统称其为“谣言”，并表示：“如果他们这样做，我们就会战斗。”
他补充道：“我们对伊朗正在发生的事情了解很多。我们知道他们所说的一切。我们知道他们是谁，他们在哪里。我们会查明真相的。”
在回答有关与万斯不和的报道的问题时，特朗普表示，副总统将共和党崩溃归咎于伊朗战争的言论是“非常准确的声明”。
“我没有说我对此不满意，”总统说。 “如果有人问我，我会补充一件事……你会再这样做吗？绝对，答案是肯定的，因为我们不能允许伊朗拥有核武器。”
特朗普被问及弗拉基米尔·普京是否真的可以被视为美国的朋友，因为俄罗斯是伊朗的亲密盟友。
“我无法与美国交谈，”他补充道，“我认为我与普京的关系非常好。这是一件非常好的事情。我与习主席的关系非常好。这是一件好事，因此我们的国家是安全的。”
他赞扬了普京，并重申了他对司法部对俄罗斯试图在 2016 年总统选举前影响美国选民的调查的不满。

title_en: The latest from Trump's press conference
title_zh: 特朗普新闻发布会的最新消息
summary: President Trump gave a wide-ranging press conference following his historic trip to Asia where he met with Chinese President Xi and Russian President Putin.
summary_zh: 特朗普总统在其历史性亚洲之行会见中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统后举行了内容广泛的新闻发布会
body_en: The latest from Trump's press conference President Trump gave a wide-ranging press conference following his historic trip to Asia where he met with Chinese President Xi and Russian President Putin.
President Trump gave a wide-ranging press conference following his historic trip to Asia where he met with Chinese President Xi and Russian President Putin.

President Trump returned to Washington after his three-day trip to Asia and took questions from the White House today. The trip included the first ever three-way meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. But there was little in the way of agreements on key global issues.
PRESIDENT DONALD TRUMP: The United States entered this trip from a position of unmatched economic and diplomatic strength.

CHANG: Well, all of this raises questions about the staying power of Trump's America-first approach and America's future role in the world. Joining us now is NPR White House correspondent Franco Ordoñez, who is in the room, and we have NPR national security correspondent Greg Myre. Hello to both of you.
CHANG: All right. So, Franco, did the president make any news in this press conference?

ORDOÑEZ: Yeah, I mean, not really. I mean, it was really a very meandering talk, starting off with highlights of his first two years in office. And then he probably spent about 30 minutes talking about his time abroad and, you know, recounting his relationship with Xi and Putin. He did say, though, that he and Xi had made some agreements about putting in guardrails - that's the word he used - with artificial intelligence, which he calls super intelligence. Here he is there.

TRUMP: It's not artificial intelligence. It's not artificial. It's super. Problem is, it may be too super. So President Xi and I agree that we're going to do some joint guardrails, the two of us, 'cause there really is no third place.

ORDOÑEZ: Now, of course, details are scarce, but the idea of guardrails is notable because Trump has pretty - previously, at least, been pretty allergic to any restrictions on developing AI. I mean, he has repeatedly said he's wanted to maintain a U.S. advantage over China.
CHANG: Right. OK, well, Greg, Trump had some things to say about chip sales to China and the whole Nvidia fallout, right? What struck you about his answers there?

MYRE: Yeah, I mean, Trump says he wants the U.S. to keep the lead in AI, as Franco just noted. And he also said he won't allow U.S. companies to build AI data centers outside the U.S. However, Trump is the one allowing Nvidia to sell advanced chips to China. Nvidia's Jensen Huang lobbied Trump last year and persuaded the president to allow these sales. And just yesterday, the House Foreign Affairs Committee released a list of requests this year by Nvidia and another chipmaker, AMD, to sell chips to Chinese company - companies. As of May this year, the Trump administration approved the sale of nearly 900,000 advanced chips, and they include big names like Alibaba and Tencent. And those two companies are also on a Pentagon list of Chinese firms that are linked to the Chinese military. So what does Trump actually want here? Does he want Nvidia to keep selling those chips to China, or does he want to block those sales?
CHANG: Good questions. Well, Trump was also asked about the whole change in leadership over cybersecurity, right? What did we learn there?

MYRE: Yeah, Trump fired the White House Cybersecurity Director Sean Carncross, and at the press conference today, he said, I don't think that person was good enough. Now, he's being replaced by Kirsten Davies, who's been the chief information officer at the Defense Department. And this is certainly an important position, but it's a policy position, not a hands on operational position.

The agency that's really important here is CISA, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, which deals with election security and protecting government networks from cyberattacks. And this agency has not had a director since Trump became president almost two years ago. Now, as it happens, Trump's nomination to lead the agency, Michael LoSapio, had a Senate confirmation hearing yesterday. He was grilled by Democratic senators. He was asked who won the 2020 presidential election. He refused to answer. He was asked if the Capitol was attacked on January 6, 2021, and he said he didn't think it was an attack. So it's not clear that he'll be confirmed, but whoever winds up in this position will be in charge of election security in 2028.

CHANG: Interesting. OK, Franco, back to this meeting with Xi and Putin, which was designed to demonstrate American power, right? Do you think it also may have opened the door for allies to turn away from the U.S.?

ORDOÑEZ: Yeah, I mean, very much designed to demonstrate American power, but I also think it does show that power and influence are not the same thing. I mean, Trump was asked today if Putin, who he called his friend, was also America's friend.

ORDOÑEZ: You know, he really couldn't answer that. But he did continue to make the case that his relationship with Putin would reap benefits for America, though we haven't really seen that yet. You know, the war in Ukraine continues to rage on. But we are seeing allies start to build alliances with other nations as, you know, confidence in the U.S. falters, and they look to reduce their dependence on the U.S.
CHANG: Well, great. What about progress when it comes to Iran? Did anything come out of this trip on that front?

MYRE: The short answer is no. There's no indication the war, now nearly nine months old, was discussed in any great detail on the trip. Trump did mention it briefly at the news conference. He said what he said many times before - Iran can't have a nuclear weapon and that Iran does want to make a deal. The one significant development in recent days has been increased Iranian attacks on oil tankers and Gulf countries.
body_zh: 特朗普新闻发布会的最新消息 特朗普总统在其历史性的亚洲之行会见了中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统普京后，举行了一场内容广泛的新闻发布会。
特朗普总统在进行历史性的亚洲之行后举行了内容广泛的新闻发布会，并会见了中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统普京。
特朗普总统结束为期三天的亚洲之行返回华盛顿，并于今天接受白宫提问。此行包括与中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统普京的首次三方会晤。但在关键的全球问题上几乎没有达成一致。
唐纳德·特朗普总统：美国以无与伦比的经济和外交实力参加此次访问。
张：嗯，所有这些都引发了人们对特朗普美国优先方针的持久力以及美国未来在世界上的角色的质疑。现在加入我们的是 NPR 白宫记者 Franco Ordoñez，他也在房间里，还有 NPR 国家安全记者 Greg Myre。你们俩好。
张：好的。那么，佛朗哥，总统在这次新闻发布会上有透露什么消息吗？
奥多涅斯：是的，我的意思是，不是真的。我的意思是，这确实是一次非常曲折的谈话，从他上任头两年的亮点开始。然后他可能花了大约 30 分钟谈论他在国外的经历，以及你知道的，讲述他与习近平和普京的关系。不过，他确实表示，他和习近平就人工智能（他称之为超级智能）安装​​护栏（这是他用的词）达成了一些协议。他就在那里。
特朗普：这不是人工智能。这不是人工的。太棒了。问题是，它可能太超级了。因此，习主席和我同意，我们两个人要共同做一些护栏，因为真的没有第三个地方。
奥多涅斯：当然，现在细节很少，但护栏的想法值得注意，因为特朗普——至少以前——对发展人工智能的任何限制非常敏感。我的意思是，他一再表示他希望保持美国对中国的优势。
张：对。好吧，格雷格，特朗普对向中国销售芯片以及整个英伟达的影响有一些话要说，对吧？他的回答让你印象深刻的是什么？

MYRE：是的，我的意思是，正如佛朗哥刚刚指出的那样，特朗普表示他希望美国在人工智能领域保持领先地位。他还表示，他不会允许美国公司在美国境外建立人工智能数据中心。然而，特朗普却允许英伟达向中国出售先进芯片。英伟达的黄仁勋去年游说特朗普并说服总统允许这些销售。就在昨天，众议院外交事务委员会公布了英伟达和另一家芯片制造商AMD今年向中国公司出售芯片的请求清单。截至今年5月，特朗普政府已批准销售近90万颗先进芯片，其中包括阿里巴巴和腾讯等大牌企业。这两家公司也在五角大楼列出的与中国军方有联系的中国公司名单上。那么特朗普到底想要什么呢？他是希望英伟达继续向中国销售这些芯片，还是想阻止这些销售？
张：好问题。好吧，特朗普还被问及网络安全领导层的整个变化，对吧？我们在那里学到了什么？
迈尔：是的，特朗普解雇了白宫网络安全总监肖恩·康克罗斯，他在今天的新闻发布会上说，我认为那个人不够好。现在，他被国防部首席信息官克尔斯滕·戴维斯 (Kirsten Davies) 接替。这当然是一个重要的立场，但这是一个政策立场，而不是实际操作立场。

这里真正重要的机构是 CISA，即网络安全和基础设施安全局，负责处理选举安全并保护政府网络免受网络攻击。自特朗普近两年前就任总统以来，该机构一直没有主任。现在，碰巧的是，特朗普提名的该机构负责人迈克尔·洛萨皮奥（Michael LoSapio）昨天在参议院举行了确认听证会。他受到民主党参议员的盘问。他被问到谁赢得了 2020 年总统选举。他拒绝回答。当被问及国会大厦是否在 2021 年 1 月 6 日遭到袭击时，他说他不认为这是一次袭击。因此，尚不清楚他是否会得到确认，但无论谁最终担任这一职务，都将负责 2028 年的选举安全。
张：有趣。好吧，佛朗哥，回到这次与习近平和普京的会面，这次会面的目的是展示美国的实力，对吧？您是否认为这也可能为盟友远离美国打开了大门？
奥尔多内斯：是的，我的意思是，这很大程度上是为了展示美国的实力，但我也认为这确实表明权力和影响力不是同一回事。我的意思是，特朗普今天被问到，他称之为朋友的普京是否也是美国的朋友。
奥尔多内斯：你知道，他真的无法回答这个问题。但他确实继续证明他与普京的关系将为美国带来好处，尽管我们还没有真正看到这一点。要知道，乌克兰战事仍在继续。但我们看到盟友开始与其他国家建立联盟，因为人们对美国的信心动摇，他们希望减少对美国的依赖。
张：嗯，太好了。伊朗问题的进展如何？这次旅行在这方面有什么收获吗？
MYRE：简短的回答是否定的。没有任何迹象表明这次旅行中对已经进行了近九个月的战争进行了任何详细的讨论。特朗普在新闻发布会上确实简短地提到了这一点。他说出了他之前多次说过的话——伊朗不能拥有核武器，而且伊朗确实希望达成协议。最近几天的一项重大进展是伊朗对油轮和海湾国家的袭击有所增加。

title_en: New Democratic governors race to deliver relief on costs
title_zh: 新民主党州长竞相减轻成本
summary: The newly elected state executives are plotting solutions on health care, housing and energy.
summary_zh: 新当选的州政府官员正在制定医疗保健、住房和能源方面的解决方案。
body_en: PARK CITY, Utah — Cost-of-living concerns fueled Democrats to victory this month. Now they’re preparing to do something about it.

As newly elected governors gathered for a job training conference hosted by the National Governors Association, conversations among the Democrat-heavy group often turned to the economic woes in their states — and the necessity to get something done quickly.

“What are the things that we can do — not in the first 100 days, but in the first 100 hours — that can start bringing some relief to the American people?” Wes Moore, the National Governors Association chair and Maryland governor, said in an interview with POLITICO.

Health care and home costs topped the target list. Several newly elected Democratic governors — Jocelyn Benson in Michigan, Keisha Lance Bottoms in Georgia, Deb Haaland in New Mexico and Rob Sand in Iowa — plan to take action to lower health costs, ranging from caps on prescription drug prices to expanding Medicaid coverage, within days of taking office. California Gov.-elect Xavier Becerra promised to spur affordable housing construction. His Nevada counterpart, Aaron Ford, said he plans to limit corporations purchasing private homes, and is preparing a day-one executive order to task every state agency with “finding ways to put money back in people's pockets.”

“You hear people signing executive orders to make things easier for businesses, cut regulations, and make it easier to do business. I think that's cool, that's fine, that's dandy,” Ford said in an interview. “But if you can do it for businesses, you can do it for people, too.”

Affordability was, far and away, the top issue for voters this cycle. Results from The POLITICO Poll, conducted just days after the midterm elections, found a 47% plurality of Americans — including 59% of Democratic voters and 41% of Republicans — said affordability and the economy were among the main issues driving their vote.

Democrats’ tsunami washed over governors’ mansions across the nation: They won 24 of the 36 governor’s races held this month, flipping red states like Texas, Alaska and Ohio, and will hold 30 of the 50 governorships nationwide next year — the most in three decades.

These governors and soon-to-be governors will be buoyed by a boon of Democrats in their statehouses: Democrats won unified control of government in Michigan, Minnesota, Nevada and Wisconsin; in North Carolina, Democrats flipped the House for the first time in 16 years and broke Republicans’ supermajority in the Senate.

As several inches of snow descended on the Wasatch Front and blanketed the glitzy ski resort in Park City this week, the newly elected governors sheltered inside the NGA’s New Governors Leadership Forum — colloquially called “baby governors’ school.” At the two-day seminar, the incoming state executives and their teams attended seminars and workshops, mingled over hors d'oeuvres and heard from current and former governors on what to expect.

Former President Bill Clinton, sitting spread-legged in a Team USA sweater Thursday, dished to a room full of governors on his book recommendations (“The Social Conquest of Earth” by E.O. Wilson), fun facts (“The combined weight of ants on earth exceeds the combined weight of all the people on earth!”) and political predictions (“I think if President Trump gets closer to leaving, he may get more interested in leaving actual legacies in forms other than buildings.”)

Clinton, who chaired the NGA when he served as governor of Arkansas, also offered some advice to the newly electeds: “The most important thing is that you and your Cabinet and your office and your organizations out in the state know what your priorities are and know what your progress is.”

Governors will face a steep climb to deliver immediate relief to Americans. Economic forces are national and international, and much of the past year’s price spikes, from fuel to food to energy, can be tied to the Iran war.

Bottoms said she will immediately begin to prepare Georgia agencies for Medicaid expansion, and expects the state legislature — with Democrats now in control of the state House, while Republicans still control the state Senate — to cooperate.
“I do believe this is an issue we will get bipartisan support on,” she told POLITICO.

In addition to his Day-One executive order, Ford says he plans to work with the Nevada legislature to sign bills in his first 30 days on expanding free public school meals, lowering the cost of prescription drugs to the Medicaid negotiated price and limiting corporations’ ability to buy private homes.

Benson said she has already reached out to the Trump administration about tariffs, which includes a 50% tariff on most Canadian exports and have disproportionately impacted Michiganders. She said she has not yet heard back, but “the point is I have reached out, and I do hope to have that conversation.”
She also emphasized her focus on lowering health care costs. “That's life or death for so many families,” Benson said.
Megan Messerly and Adam Wren contributed reporting.
body_zh: 犹他州帕克城——对生活成本的担忧促使民主党在本月取得胜利。现在他们正准备对此采取行动。
当新当选的州长聚集在一起参加由全国州长协会主办的职业培训会议时，以民主党为主的团体之间的谈话经常转向本州的经济困境，以及迅速完成某些事情的必要性。
“我们可以做哪些事情——不是在前 100 天，而是在前 100 小时——可以开始为美国人民带来一些缓解？”全国州长协会主席、马里兰州州长韦斯·摩尔在接受《POLITICO》采访时表示。

医疗保健和家庭费用位居目标清单之首。几位新当选的民主党州长——密歇根州的乔斯林·本森、佐治亚州的凯莎·兰斯·博顿斯、新墨西哥州的德布·哈兰德和爱荷华州的罗布·桑德——计划在上任后几天内采取行动降低医疗成本，从处方药价格上限到扩大医疗补助覆盖范围。当选加州州长泽维尔·贝塞拉承诺刺激经济适用房建设。内华达州同行亚伦·福特表示，他计划限制企业购买私人住宅，并正在准备一项第一天的行政命令，要求每个州机构“想办法让钱回到人们的口袋里”。
“你会听到人们签署行政命令，让企业变得更容易，减少监管，让做生意更容易。我认为这很酷，很好，这太棒了，”福特在接受采访时说。 “但如果你能为企业做到这一点，你也可以为人们做到这一点。”
负担能力无疑是本周期选民的首要问题。中期选举几天后进行的 POLITICO 民意调查显示，47% 的美国人（包括 59% 的民主党选民和 41% 的共和党选民）表示，负担能力和经济是推动他们投票的主要问题之一。
民主党的海啸席卷了全国各地的州长官邸：他们赢得了本月举行的 36 场州长竞选中的 24 场，击败了得克萨斯州、阿拉斯加州和俄亥俄州等红州，并将在明年获得全国 50 个州长职位中的 30 个——这是三十年来最多的一次。
这些州长和即将上任的州长将受到州议会中民主党人的支持：民主党赢得了密歇根州、明尼苏达州、内华达州和威斯康星州政府的统一控制权；民主党赢得了密歇根州、明尼苏达州、内华达州和威斯康星州的政府统一控制权；在北卡罗来纳州，民主党16年来首次翻转众议院，打破了共和党在参议院的绝对多数席位。
本周，瓦萨奇前线降下数英寸厚的积雪，覆盖了帕克城华丽的滑雪胜地，新当选的州长们躲在 NGA 的新州长领导力论坛（俗称“婴儿州长学校”）内。在为期两天的研讨会上，即将上任的州行政人员及其团队参加了研讨会和讲习班，一边享用开胃小菜，一边听取现任和前任州长的意见。
周四，前总统比尔·克林顿穿着美国队毛衣，张开双腿坐着，向满屋子的州长推荐他的书籍（E.O.威尔逊的《社会征服地球》）、有趣的事实（“地球上蚂蚁的总重量超过了地球上所有人的总重量！”）和政治预测（“我认为，如果特朗普总统离任越来越近，他可能会对以建筑物以外的形式留下实际遗产更感兴趣。”）
担任阿肯色州州长期间担任 NGA 主席的克林顿也向新当选的人提出了一些建议：“最重要的是，你和你的内阁、你的办公室以及你在该州的组织知道你的优先事项是什么，知道你的进展是什么。”
州长们将面临陡峭的攀升，以立即为美国人提供救济。经济力量是国内和国际的，去年从燃料到食品再到能源的价格上涨大部分都与伊朗战争有关。
博托姆斯表示，她将立即开始为佐治亚州各机构扩大医疗补助计划做好准备，并预计州立法机构（目前民主党控制着州众议院，而共和党仍控制着州参议院）进行合作。
“我确实相信这是一个我们会得到两党支持的问题，”她告诉《政治》杂志。
福特表示，除了第一天的行政命令外，他还计划在上任后的 30 天内与内华达州立法机构合作签署法案，扩大公立学校的免费餐食，将处方药的成本降低至医疗补助协议的谈判价格，并限制企业购买私人住宅的能力。
本森表示，她已经就关税问题与特朗普政府进行了接触，其中包括对大多数加拿大出口产品征收 50% 的关税，这对密歇根人造成了不成比例的影响。她说她还没有收到回复，但“重点是我已经联系了，我确实希望进行对话。”
她还强调了她对降低医疗保健成本的关注。 “这对许多家庭来说是生死攸关的事情，”本森说。
梅根·梅瑟利和亚当·雷恩贡献了报道。

title_en: A second judge blocks Trump's arch, saying it's unlikely to succeed in court
title_zh: 第二名法官挡住了特朗普的拱门，称其不太可能在法庭上成功
summary: A federal judge in Virginia said she will issue a preliminary injunction against Trump's arch, going a step further than the D.C. federal judge who temporarily blocked construction earlier this week.
summary_zh: 弗吉尼亚州的一名联邦法官表示，她将针对特朗普的拱门发布初步禁令，这比华盛顿特区的联邦法官更进一步。
body_en: Trump arch blocked by Virginia judge A federal judge in Virginia said she will issue a preliminary injunction against Trump's arch, going a step further than the D.C. federal judge who temporarily blocked construction earlier this week.
President Trump holds up a model of his proposed triumphal arch at a White House event in Oct. 2025. Two different federal judges have ruled against it this week. John McDonnell/AP hide caption
A federal judge in Virginia plans to issue a preliminary injunction blocking President Trump's triumphal arch indefinitely.

District Judge Leonie Brinkema said during a Friday hearing that she would grant the request of the county board of Arlington, Va., which sued over the arch in October. Democracy Forward, the nonprofit representing the plaintiffs, confirmed the ruling in a statement shared with NPR.
Judges have put Trump's arch and golf course on hold, but only for a matter of days

"We are pleased that the court has recognized the irreparable harm that will come to people who live and work in Arlington and stopped the massive vanity project while our case is heard and considered by the court," said senior counsel Kate Talmor.
Justice Department spokesperson Matthew Nies told NPR it will appeal the decision immediately.

The 250-foot arch would be built in Memorial Circle, which is part of D.C. but sits on the Virginia side of the Potomac River, a short distance from both Arlington National Cemetery and Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, both in Arlington.

Arlington County has argued that the arch would "cause significant harm" to its residents in multiple ways, including increasing noise and air pollution and "clogging thoroughfares needed for emergency transport services." And it said an arch that doubles as a military complex — as Trump has suggested — would pose public safety risks and require additional county resources to manage.

Arlington also argues the arch would disrupt historic sightlines between Arlington National Cemetery and D.C.'s National Mall , and pose logistical challenges for the roughly 24 to 27 funerals the cemetery holds every weekday. The county also has concerns about air and road traffic, saying construction-related delays could cause more accidents and disrupt emergency vehicles far beyond the traffic circle.

"In the last 60 days, Arlington police, fire, and emergency units have responded to approximately 200 incidents in the area surrounding the Circle, including traffic stops and assisting with unconscious persons within Arlington National Cemetery," they wrote. "And the visitors the Arch is intended to attract will increase demand for those same emergency services."
Kennedy relatives join the fight against Trump's arch, alleging harm to JFK's grave

The plaintiffs, like many critics of the arch , accused the Trump administration of rushing through federally mandated environmental reviews and failing to consider alternatives. The National Park Service has defended the federal review process — which ended in approval earlier this month — and said building the arch somewhere else would defeat its purpose .

"The County brings this lawsuit to halt the agency's feverish pace toward construction of the Arch and to ensure that the 'hard look' mandated by [the National Environmental Preservation Act] is completed before the agency commences disruptive and harmful ground-disturbing activities," the plaintiffs wrote last month.

NPR has reached out to the White House for comment. Spokesperson Davis Ingle told NPR earlier this week that the administration will "continue making the case for this beautiful and fitting monument and are confident we will be fully vindicated as this litigation proceeds."
Brinkema, an appointee of President Clinton, is the second judge to rule against the arch this week.

On Wednesday, D.C. District Judge Tanya Chutkan extended a restraining order that prevents the Trump administration from breaking ground through Dec. 3 while she considers the underlying legal arguments.
Democrats want to stop Trump's arch, golf course and more. What are their options?

That case was brought earlier this year by a group that includes Vietnam War veterans and was joined by the governments of D.C. and Virginia last month. Nine Kennedy family members moved to get involved last week.
body_zh: 弗吉尼亚州法官封锁特朗普拱门 弗吉尼亚州一名联邦法官表示，她将对特朗普拱门发布初步禁令，这比本周早些时候暂时阻止施工的华盛顿特区联邦法官更进一步。
特朗普总统在 2025 年 10 月的白宫活动中举起了他提议的凯旋门模型。本周，两名不同的联邦法官做出了反对的裁决。约翰·麦克唐纳/美联社隐藏标题栏
弗吉尼亚州的一名联邦法官计划发布初步禁令，无限期阻止特朗普总统的凯旋门。
地区法官莱昂妮·布林克玛 (Leonie Brinkema) 在周五的听证会上表示，她将批准弗吉尼亚州阿灵顿县委员会的请求，该县委员会于 10 月份就拱门提起了诉讼。代表原告的非营利组织“民主前进”在与 NPR 分享的一份声明中证实了这一裁决。
法官暂停了特朗普的拱门和高尔夫球场，但只持续了几天
高级律师凯特·塔尔莫 (Kate Talmor) 表示：“我们很高兴法院认识到这将对阿灵顿生活和工作的人们造成不可挽回的伤害，并在法院审理和审议我们的案件期间停止了大规模的虚荣工程。”
司法部发言人马修·尼斯 (Matthew Nies) 告诉 NPR，司法部将立即对这一决定提出上诉。
这座 250 英尺高的拱门将建在纪念圆环内，该纪念环是华盛顿特区的一部分，但位于波托马克河的弗吉尼亚一侧，距离阿灵顿国家公墓和罗纳德·里根华盛顿国家机场都很近。
阿灵顿县辩称，这座拱门将以多种方式对其居民“造成重大伤害”，包括增加噪音和空气污染以及“堵塞紧急交通服务所需的通道”。它还表示，正如特朗普所建议的那样，一座兼作军事设施的拱门将构成公共安全风险，并需要额外的县资源来管理。
阿灵顿还认为，这座拱门会扰乱阿灵顿国家公墓和华盛顿特区国家广场之间的历史视线，并给该公墓每周举办大约 24 至 27 场葬礼带来后勤挑战。该县还对空中和道路交通表示担忧，称与施工相关的延误可能会导致更多事故，并扰乱远离交通圈的紧急车辆。
他们写道：“在过去 60 天里，阿灵顿警察、消防和应急部门对圆环周边地区约 ​​200 起事件做出了反应，包括在阿灵顿国家公墓内拦截交通并协助失去知觉的人员。” “拱门旨在吸引的游客将增加对这些紧急服务的需求。”
肯尼迪亲属加入反对特朗普拱门的斗争，声称肯尼迪坟墓遭到破坏
与许多对该拱门的批评者一样，原告指责特朗普政府匆忙进行联邦政府规定的环境审查，而没有考虑替代方案。国家公园管理局为联邦审查程序进行了辩护——该程序于本月初获得批准——并表示在其他地方建造拱门将达不到其目的。
原告上个月写道：“县提起这起诉讼是为了阻止该机构建造拱门的狂热步伐，并确保在该机构开始破坏性和有害的地面扰动活动之前完成[国家环境保护法]规定的‘严格审查’。”
NPR 已联系白宫请其置评。发言人戴维斯·英格尔本周早些时候告诉美国公共广播电台，政府将“继续为这座美丽而合适的纪念碑辩护，并相信随着诉讼的进行，我们将得到充分证明。”
克林顿总统任命的布林克马是本周第二位做出反对拱门裁决的法官。
周三，华盛顿地区法官塔尼娅·查特坎 (Tanya Chutkan) 延长了一项限制令，阻止特朗普政府在 12 月 3 日之前破土动工，同时她正在考虑潜在的法律论据。
民主党人希望阻止特朗普的拱门、高尔夫球场等。他们的选择是什么？
今年早些时候，一个包括越南战争退伍军人在内的团体提起了这一诉讼，上个月华盛顿特区和弗吉尼亚州政府也加入了该诉讼。肯尼迪家族的九名成员上周也参与其中。

title_en: Trump initially accepted the midterm results, but most GOP voters doubt they were fair
title_zh: 特朗普最初接受了中期结果，但大多数共和党选民怀疑这些结果是否公平
summary: Less than half of Republicans nationwide considered the midterm elections "free and fair," according to new polling.
summary_zh: 根据新的民意调查，全国不到一半的共和党人认为中期选举“自由和公平”。
body_en: A firefighter walks past voting booths at a firehouse serving as a polling location in Detroit on Nov. 3. Spencer Platt/Getty Images hide caption
President Trump may have initially accepted the results of his party's midterm losses , but data released Friday shows there is still broad distrust in the elections process among Republicans.

Less than half of Republican voters nationwide considered the midterm elections "free and fair," according to new polling by the University of California San Diego. Just 52% of Republicans said they trusted votes were counted accurately.
In comparison, after the 2024 election that Trump won, more than 80% of Republicans said they had confidence in the vote-counting process.
While trust in elections often dips for voters of the losing party, the GOP has seen bigger swings in confidence in recent years, as Trump has falsely claimed that U.S. elections are corrupt.

"There are still a lot of people who remain unconvinced that they can trust elections," said Thad Kousser, a co-director of UC San Diego's Center for Transparent and Trusted Elections. "And they're predominantly located in one [political] party."

Overall, a wide majority — 66% — of Americans said they think the midterms were fair. That represents an improvement from before the election , when less than half of U.S. adults said they expected free and fair contests.

But that post-election increase in trust was buoyed by Democrats and independents — many of whom worried before Election Day about potential federal interference at the polls that didn't come to pass .

"It would be a mistake to [look at the 66%] and think, 'Oh, everyone has a pretty good view of the election,'" said Lauren Prather, also a co-director of UC San Diego's election center. "It really buries the lede a little bit about the partisan gap."
GOP state officials push to revive Trump's mail voting restrictions for 2028 election
The Trump administration's voter roll crusade could continue
The widespread doubt among Republicans may be a reality check for those wondering whether Trump's brand of election denial has run its course in American politics.

On the one hand, there will be fewer politicians who deny or question election results in office next year. And the vast majority of election-denying candidates running for positions involved in overseeing statewide elections lost their races this year, according to tracking by the advocacy group States United Action.
Election experts have also celebrated as Trump and high-profile losing candidates on the ballot this year conceded their losses.
"Sure, I'll accept [the results]," Trump told Fox News' Bret Baier on election night, as it became clear Democrats would retake the House and Senate. "Why wouldn't I?"
But just a few days later, he began conspiracy theorizing about those same results.
"Does anybody really believe that this 'Election' was honest," Trump posted online .

The new polling from UC San Diego shows that among Republicans, there still may be a receptive audience to such claims. When asked if politicians are discussing voter fraud too much, too little or about the right amount, just 15% of Republicans answered "too much."

"There is both demand among the Republican base for continued focus on this issue, and as we saw even after the election, politicians are continuing to supply it," Kousser said. "As long as those two dynamics are there, there's still going to be a market for these concerns."
body_zh: 11 月 3 日，底特律，一名消防员走过作为投票地点的消防站的投票站。Spencer Platt/Getty Images 隐藏标题栏
特朗普总统最初可能已经接受了本党中期选举失利的结果，但周五公布的数据显示，共和党人对选举进程仍存在广泛的不信任。
根据加州大学圣地亚哥分校的最新民意调查，全国不到一半的共和党选民认为中期选举“自由和公平”。只有 52% 的共和党人表示，他们相信计票结果是准确的。
相比之下，特朗普赢得2024年大选后，超过80%的共和党人表示对计票过程有信心。
虽然失败政党的选民对选举的信任度经常下降，但近年来共和党的信心波动更大，因为特朗普错误地声称美国选举存在腐败。
加州大学圣地亚哥分校透明和可信选举中心联席主任萨德·库塞尔表示：“仍然有很多人不相信选举可以信任。” “而且他们主要属于一个[政治]政党。”
总体而言，绝大多数（66%）美国人表示，他们认为中期选举是公平的。这比选举前有所改善，当时不到一半的美国成年人表示他们期待自由和公平的竞争。
但选举后信任度的提高得到了民主党人和独立人士的提振——他们中的许多人在选举日之前担心联邦可能对民意调查进行干预，但这种干预并未实现。
加州大学圣地亚哥分校选举中心联合主任劳伦·普拉瑟 (Lauren Prather) 表示：“（看看 66% 的人）并认为‘哦，每个人都对选举有很好的看法’，这是错误的。” “这确实掩盖了一些关于党派分歧的争论。”
共和党州官员推动恢复特朗普对 2028 年大选的邮件投票限制
特朗普政府的选民名册运动可能会继续
共和党人普遍存在的疑虑可能是对那些想知道特朗普否认选举的做法是否已经在美国政治中走到尽头的人们的现实检验。
一方面，明年在任时否认或质疑选举结果的政客将会减少。根据倡导组织“联合行动”的追踪，绝大多数竞选参与监督全州选举职位的拒绝选举的候选人今年都输掉了竞选。
选举专家们也庆祝了特朗普和今年投票中高调落选的候选人承认自己的失败。
“当然，我会接受（结果），”特朗普在选举之夜告诉福克斯新闻的布雷特·拜尔，因为民主党将重新夺回众议院和参议院已变得很明显。 “我为什么不呢？”
但仅仅几天后，他就开始对同样的结果进行阴谋论。
“有人真的相信这次‘选举’是诚实的吗？”特朗普在网上发帖称。
加州大学圣地亚哥分校的最新民意调查显示，在共和党人中，可能仍然有一些人接受这种说法。当被问及政客们对选民欺诈的讨论是否太多、太少或恰到好处时，只有 15% 的共和党人回答“太多”。
库塞尔说：“共和党基础选民要求继续关注这个问题，而且正如我们所看到的，即使在选举之后，政客们也在继续提供这一点。” “只要这两种动力存在，这些担忧仍然会有市场。”

title_en: Fired White House press secretary Katie Zacharia under California state bar investigation
title_zh: 加州律师协会调查解雇白宫新闻秘书凯蒂·扎卡里亚
summary: Zacharia’s spokesperson called allegations she falsely represented herself as an attorney ‘baseless’ US politics live – latest updates Katie Zacharia, the former White House press secretary hired and fired in the same week , is under investigation by the state
summary_zh: 扎卡里亚的发言人称她谎称自己是一名律师的指控“毫无根据”美国政治直播——最新更新凯蒂·扎卡里亚，
body_en: Fired White House press secretary Katie Zacharia under California state bar investigation | Trump administration
Zacharia’s spokesperson called allegations she falsely represented herself as an attorney ‘baseless’

Katie Zacharia, the former White House press secretary hired and fired in the same week , is under investigation by the state bar of California for claiming to be a lawyer despite never passing the bar exam.

Earlier this month, the state bar of California informed Campaign for Accountability, a non-profit watchdog group, that it had assigned an investigator and legal adviser to investigate Zacharia after the organization filed a complaint.

Before her short stint as Donald Trump ’s press secretary, Zacharia repeatedly represented herself as a lawyer on cable news programs and had claimed on her LinkedIn profile that she served as the general counsel for a non-profit organization in California.
Trump also identified Zacharia as an “attorney” when announcing her appointment.
While Zacharia received a law degree from Pepperdine University in 2011, she never passed the bar exam in California or any other US state .

“Zacharia may have thought she was just playing a lawyer on TV, but by repeatedly holding herself out as an attorney on news programs, she was pretending to have authority she lacks,” Michelle Kuppersmith, the director of the Campaign for Accountability, said in a statement.
“We’re pleased the California bar is taking this matter seriously and investigating,” Kuppersmith added.

A spokesperson for Zacharia said in a statement to the Guardian: “These are baseless allegations. This complaint is politically motivated and a clear waste of the state bar’s time and resources. We are confident it will be dismissed with no finding of wrongdoing.”

Zacharia previously defended describing herself as a “lawyer”, claiming there was a difference between a “lawyer” and an “attorney”, a title reserved for those licensed to practice law. In her email to the Guardian, Zacharia linked to an American Bar Association Journal article distinguishing the two terms.
A spokesperson for the state bar of California said it was aware of media reports about “non-licensee Katie Zacharia” and that investigations were confidential.

“The state bar notes that neither the submission of a complaint nor the conduct of an investigation constitutes a finding that a non-licensee has engaged in unauthorized practice of law in violation of California statutes,” the spokesperson said.
The Campaign for Accountability had submitted a complaint to the state bar of California in mid-October.

“In California, calling yourself a lawyer without a license isn’t puffery; it’s a crime. The state bar should investigate whether Ms Zacharia has misled the public about her credentials and hold her accountable if she has,” the non-profit watchdog organization wrote in their complaint.

Zacharia became the shortest-serving White House press secretary when she replaced Karoline Leavitt in mid-October for just five days. From the start, she struggled to fit into the role, stumbling over words during her first press briefing and only taking questions from predominantly conservative media outlets.
body_zh: 加州律师协会调查解雇白宫新闻秘书凯蒂·扎卡里亚 (Katie Zacharia)特朗普政府
扎卡里亚的发言人称，关于她虚假冒充律师的指控“毫无根据”
前白宫新闻秘书凯蒂·扎卡里亚(Katie Zacharia)在同一周被聘用并被解雇，她因从未通过律师考试而自称是律师，正在接受加利福尼亚州律师协会的调查。
本月早些时候，加州律师协会通知非营利监督组织“问责运动”，在该组织提出投诉后，它已指派一名调查员和法律顾问对该组织进行调查。
在短暂担任唐纳德·特朗普的新闻秘书之前，扎卡里亚多次在有线电视新闻节目中以律师的身份出现，并在她的 LinkedIn 个人资料中声称，她曾担任加利福尼亚州一家非营利组织的总法律顾问。
特朗普在宣布任命扎卡里亚时还称她为“律师”。
虽然扎卡里亚于 2011 年获得佩珀代因大学法律学位，但她从未通过加利福尼亚州或美国任何其他州的律师考试。
“扎卡里亚可能以为她只是在电视上扮演律师，但通过在新闻节目中反复表明自己是律师，她假装拥有自己所缺乏的权威，”问责运动主任米歇尔·库珀史密斯在一份声明中表示。
“我们很高兴加州酒吧认真对待此事并进行调查，”库珀史密斯补充道。
扎卡里亚的发言人在给《卫报》的一份声明中表示：“这些都是毫无根据的指控。这项投诉是出于政治动机，明显浪费了州律师协会的时间和资源。我们相信，在没有发现任何不当行为的情况下，它将被驳回。”
扎卡里亚此前曾为自己的“律师”身份进行辩护，声称“律师”和“律师”是有区别的，“律师”是为那些获得律师执业资格的人保留的头衔。扎卡里亚在给《卫报》的电子邮件中链接到美国律师协会杂志上一篇区分这两个术语的文章。
加州律师协会发言人表示，他们知道媒体有关“非持照人凯蒂·扎卡里亚”的报道，并且调查是保密的。
该发言人表示：“州律师协会指出，提交投诉或进行调查均不构成非持照人从事违反加州法规的未经授权的执业行为的认定。”
问责运动已于十月中旬向加利福尼亚州律师协会提交了一份投诉。
“在加州，自称没有执照的律师并不是吹嘘；而是犯罪。州律师协会应该调查扎卡里亚女士是否在她的资质方面误导了公众，如果有的话，追究她的责任，”非营利监管组织在投诉中写道。
扎卡里亚于 10 月中旬接替卡罗琳·莱维特，任期仅五天，成为任职时间最短的白宫新闻秘书。从一开始，她就很难融入这个角色，在第一次新闻发布会上结结巴巴，只回答主要保守派媒体的问题。

body_en: Construction of ⁠Trump’s ‌proposed ‘triumphal arch’ blocked by judge | Donald Trump
Virginia judge says the US president’s pet project ​is ​a ‘rushed job’ ​that ‌lacks ​legal basis

A federal judge on Friday morning said she would issue a preliminary injunction to block construction of ⁠Donald Trump’s ‌proposed so-called “ triumphal arch ” as a huge presence near some of the most famous and sacred sites in the Washington DC area.
Judge Leonie Brinkema in Alexandria, Virginia , ​said during a ⁠hearing ​on Friday that the US president’s pet project ​was ​a “rushed job” ​that ‌lacked ​a ​legal basis.

Brinkema said the administration had not conducted proper analysis of the environmental and economic impact of the project, such as the effect on airspace at nearby Reagan Washington national airport.
“That just hasn’t been done in the case because ​it’s been such a rushed job,” the ‌judge said, according to Reuters.
Brinkema is the second federal judge to take issue with the 250ft arch that the US president hopes to install on Memorial Circle near Arlington national cemetery.

Earlier this month, Judge Tanya Chutkan in Washington temporarily blocked construction of the triumphal arch, saying the administration needed congressional approval before moving forward. Chutkan raised concerns about the costly construction as well as disruptions it could cause to traffic at the cemetery.
Chutkan extended her order this week, barring the administration from initiating any construction or demolition until the beginning of December.
Over the last year, Trump has boasted about building an arch in the middle of the nation’s capital to mark the US’s 250th anniversary.
He has sought to hurriedly build the arch, arguing it is for national security purposes because it will include a military complex.

Trump’s arch has been met with legal challenges from veterans groups, local governments and individuals such as members of the Kennedy family. Critics have taken issue with the arch’s enormous size and location, believing it would hurt the symbolic relationship between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington national cemetery.

Challengers have argued the US president needed authorization from Congress before constructing the arch. But lawyers for the administration claim they do not because Congress approved the construction of a pair of columns at the location in 1925, though the columns were never built.
On Friday, Brinkema said the administration’s argument about the 1925 congressional authorization of columns was weak.
“It hurts your credibility with the court by focusing on that,” the judge told government lawyers. “This is a project that lacks congressional approval.”
body_zh: 特朗普提议建造的“凯旋门”被法官阻止|唐纳德·特朗普
弗吉尼亚州法官表示，美国总统的宠物项目是一项“仓促工作”，缺乏法律依据
周五早上，一名联邦法官表示，她将发布一项初步禁令，阻止在华盛顿特区一些最著名和神圣的地点附近修建唐纳德·特朗普提议的所谓“凯旋门”。
弗吉尼亚州亚历山大市的法官莱昂妮·布林克马 (Leonie Brinkema) 在周五的听证会上表示，美国总统的宠爱项目是一项“仓促工作”，缺乏法律依据。
布林克玛表示，政府没有对该项目的环境和经济影响进行适当的分析，例如对附近里根华盛顿国家机场空域的影响。
据路透社报道，法官表示：“本案并未这样做，因为这是一项非常仓促的工作。”
布林克马是第二位对美国总统希望在阿灵顿国家公墓附近的纪念圈上安装的 250 英尺拱门提出异议的联邦法官。
本月早些时候，华盛顿法官塔尼娅·查特坎(Tanya Chutkan)暂时阻止了凯旋门的建设，称政府需要国会批准才能继续建造。查特坎对耗资巨大的建设以及可能对墓地交通造成的干扰表示担忧。
Chutkan 本周延长了她的命令，禁止政府在 12 月初之前启动任何建设或拆除活动。
去年，特朗普吹嘘要在美国首都中部建造一座拱门，以纪念美国建国 250 周年。
他试图匆忙建造这座拱门，认为这是出于国家安全目的，因为它将包括一个军事设施。
特朗普的拱门遭到了退伍军人团体、地方政府和肯尼迪家族成员等个人的法律挑战。批评者对拱门的巨大尺寸和位置提出了质疑，认为这会损害林肯纪念堂和阿灵顿国家公墓之间的象征性关系。
挑战者认为，美国总统在建造拱门之前需要得到国会的授权。但政府的律师声称他们没有这样做，因为国会于 1925 年批准在该地点建造一对圆柱，尽管这些圆柱从未建成。
周五，布林克玛表示，政府关于 1925 年国会授权修建立柱的论点是站不住脚的。
法官告诉政府律师：“专注于这一点会损害你在法庭上的信誉。” “这是一个缺乏国会批准的项目。”

title_en: Trump formally ends minting of the penny after nearly 250 years of production
title_zh: 特朗普正式终止铸造近 250 年的便士
summary: The U.S. Mint, which began producing the currency in 1793, has said it costs nearly 4 cents to make each penny.
summary_zh: 美国造币厂于 1793 年开始生产这种货币，称每美分的制造成本接近 4 美分。
body_en: Trump formally ends penny minting after nearly 250 years of production
Washington is officially done with spending a pretty penny on penny production .
President Donald Trump on Friday signed the bipartisan Common Cents Act , which formally directs the federal government to stop minting the penny.
Both the House and the Senate passed the measure by voice vote, meaning no notable opposition.

“It costs nearly FOUR cents to make just one penny,” the bill’s author, Rep. Lisa McClain, R-Mich., said Sept. 29 on X a day after Senate passage . “This legislation will save $85 million per year by permanently ending penny production — it’s common sense!”
The U.S. Mint last year put the immediate annual savings of discontinuing penny production at $56 million .

The government stopped making pennies in November 2025 , nine months after Trump called for the Treasury Department to stop production , writing at the time that the process was “so wasteful!” However, the U.S. Mint said it would still produce collector versions to be produced in “limited quantities.”

The penny can still be used as legal tender “for all debts, public charges, taxes, and dues,” according to the new law. The Treasury Department said last year that the Federal Reserve will continue to recirculate the approximately 114 billion pennies that are in existence “for as long as possible.”
The new measure also provides a procedure for stores and businesses that accept cash payments to round their prices to the nearest amount divisible by 5 cents.

And, as the nickel replaces the penny at the bottom of the U.S. Mint’s currency list, that coin can now be manufactured with an inner layer of zinc and an outer layer of nickel. It is currently produced with nickel and copper, which costs more than zinc.
Congress passed the Coinage Act in 1792, and the U.S. Mint began producing the penny, known officially as the cent, the following year.
In its nearly 250 years in production, the penny has had multiple facades. It wasn’t until 1909 that it was given its modern-day face, featuring President Abraham Lincoln.

The first penny, produced in 1787, had a sundial design created by Benjamin Franklin. After the U.S. Mint took over, the penny was slightly bigger and included the image of a woman representing Liberty on one side and 15 chain links on the other.

The next penny debuted in 1857, taking on a smaller shape and displaying a flying eagle design on one side and a wreath on the other. It also changed from being 100% copper to 88% copper and 12% nickel. Two years later, an “Indian Head” design was added to one side.

The most recent design from the U.S. Mint was issued in 2010, featuring its “Union Shield” theme. It shows a shield on the tails side of the coin to represent “Lincoln’s preservation of the United States as a single country,” the U.S. Mint wrote.
Kyla Guilfoil is a breaking news reporter on the politics team for NBC News Digital.
body_zh: 特朗普正式终止铸造近 250 年的便士
华盛顿正式不再在廉价生产上花费大量资金。
唐纳德·特朗普总统周五签署了两党共同美分法案，正式指示联邦政府停止铸造美分硬币。
众议院和参议院均以口头表决方式通过了这项措施，这意味着没有明显的反对声音。
该法案的作者、密歇根州共和党众议员丽莎·麦克莱恩 (Lisa McClain) 在参议院通过后的第二天 9 月 29 日表示，“仅生产一便士就要花费近四美分”。 “这项立法将通过永久终止便士生产每年节省 8500 万美元——这是常识！”
美国造币厂去年预计，停止生产便士每年可节省 5600 万美元。
2025 年 11 月，即特朗普呼吁财政部停止生产的九个月后，政府停止了生产，当时特朗普写道，这一过程“太浪费了！”不过，美国造币厂表示，仍将生产“限量”的收藏版。
根据新法律，一分钱仍然可以用作“所有债务、公共费用、税收和会费”的法定货币。美国财政部去年表示，美联储将“尽可能长时间地”继续循环现有的约 1140 亿便士。
新措施还为接受现金付款的商店和企业提供了将价格四舍五入到可被 5 美分整除的最接近金额的程序。
而且，随着镍取代了美国造币厂货币列表中最底层的便士，该硬币现在可以用内层锌和外层镍来制造。目前它是用镍和铜生产的，其成本比锌更高。
国会于 1792 年通过了《铸币法》，次年美国造币厂开始生产便士，正式名称为美分。
在近 250 年的生产过程中，便士有多个正面。直到 1909 年，它才被赋予现代面貌，以亚伯拉罕·林肯总统为主角。
1787 年生产的第一枚便士上有本杰明·富兰克林 (Benjamin Franklin) 设计的日晷图案。美国造币厂接手后，便士的尺寸稍大一些，一侧是代表自由的女性形象，另一侧是 15 个链环。
下一便士于 1857 年首次亮相，形状较小，一侧为飞鹰图案，另一侧为花环。它还从 100% 铜变为 88% 铜和 12% 镍。两年后，一侧添加了“印第安人头像”设计。
美国造币厂的最新设计于 2010 年发行，以“联邦盾牌”为主题。美国造币厂写道，硬币尾部有一个盾牌，代表“林肯维护美国作为一个单一国家”。
Kyla Guilfoil 是 NBC News Digital 政治团队的突发新闻记者。

title_en: Trump touts meeting with Xi and Putin but offers little results
title_zh: 特朗普大肆宣扬与习近平和普京的会面，但收效甚微
summary: At a White House press conference Friday, Trump offered little in actual results of the meetings, beyond a joint statement on unity over some issues.
summary_zh: 在周五的白宫新闻发布会上，特朗普除了就某些问题发表联合声明外，几乎没有透露会议的实际结果。
body_en: President Trump speaks as Secretary of State Marco Rubio listens during a news briefing at the White House on Friday. Trump is addressing the media after returning from a visit to China where he held trilateral talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping. Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images hide caption

President Trump took to the White House briefing room Friday telling reporters his trip to Asia this week – where he met with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian leader Vladimir Putin – was a resounding success, despite offering few tangible results.

"The United States entered this trip from a position of unmatched economic and diplomatic strength," Trump said, standing at the podium with VIce President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio behind him.

But the trip resulted more in agreements to continue discussions rather than any concrete changes. The meeting with Putin and Xi, though historic as it was the first time they met, only resulted in an agreement to continue discussing reducing nuclear risks.

In Manila, where Trump met with allies before he traveled to China, Trump signed a trade agreement with Thailand. But there are still details to the deal being finalized and the document signed simply marked a "substantial conclusion" in negotiations.
Trump, Xi and Putin meet as global alliances hang in the balance

At the White House, Trump gave a wide-ranging opening statement to the press that veered from recounting his trip and who he met with, to asides about Iran, the U.S. Federal Reserve, his quest for a Nobel Peace Prize and domestic manufacturing. It was the first time he took questions from the press since being in China.

One significant change Trump announced in the middle of his press remarks was that he and XI have agreed to establish "joint guardrails" on artificial intelligence – a new move from Trump, who has been adamant that regulation over the technology would inhibit US innovation and help China lead in the global AI race. No further details about what the guardrails would look like, when they would be negotiated and released and how they would be applied between the two nations has been announced.

Trump, who said Xi also likes his term "super intelligence" rather than artificial, said, "Problem is, it may be too super. So, President Xi and I agree that we're going to do some joint guardrails, the two of us."
The announcement of future guardrails comes as Trump is facing headwinds from growing tech outages in the U.S. that ultimately led to Trump replacing the White House's cyber director.

In the briefing, Trump added that he would continue to push for the construction of data centers in the U.S. This comes after midterm election voters from both parties showed their opposition to future unfettered growth.
Trump heads to Asia to meet with Xi and Putin amid Nvidia fallout
"Make them pay your community, but take advantage. Don't shut them off," Trump said of the massive complexes that have drawn criticism from communities due to environmental and noise pollution.
He also announced penalizations against companies that try to build data centers outside the U.S.

"If it's not this country, there's somebody else outside. And we're not going to allow our companies to build data centers outside of our country. We're not going to allow that to happen," Trump said.

Trump's trip to China came as Trump's own cabinet on what approach to take toward China. Trump's Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has been in favor of selling China U.S. chips, a stance that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang shared. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has expressed a more hawkish view toward China, and Trump has acknowledged both perspectives.

The divide has become more prominent as Lutnick and Trump face backlash for their relationship to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned from his position after admitting to an affair with a woman who may be a Chinese spy.

On Friday, Trump said he only wants "older chips" to be sold to China, rather than the most cutting-edge technology the U.S. has, and he said he'd be OK with no chips going to China at all, though he pointed out the downside to that.
"You have to understand, China makes chips too," Trump said. "And if we're not going to sell them, they'll make them themselves."
body_zh: 周五在白宫举行的新闻发布会上，特朗普总统发表讲话，国务卿马可·鲁比奥在旁听。特朗普在访问中国归来后向媒体发表讲话，他在中国与俄罗斯总统普京和中国国家主席习近平举行了三边会谈。凯文迪奇/盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
特朗普总统周五在白宫新闻发布室告诉记者，他本周的亚洲之行——他会见了中国领导人习近平和俄罗斯领导人普京——尽管没有带来什么具体成果，但取得了巨大成功。
特朗普站在讲台上说道：“美国以无与伦比的经济和外交实力进入此行。”他身后是副总统万斯和国务卿马可·卢比奥。
但这次访问更多地达成了继续讨论的协议，而不是任何具体的改变。与普京和习近平的会面虽然具有历史意义，但只是达成了继续讨论减少核风险的协议。
特朗普在访问中国之前在马尼拉会见了盟友，并与泰国签署了贸易协议。但该交易仍有细节正在敲定，签署的文件只是标志着谈判的“实质性结论”。
特朗普、习近平和普京会面，全球联盟岌岌可危
在白宫，特朗普向媒体发表了内容广泛的开场白，内容从叙述他的行程和会见的人，转向谈论伊朗、美联储、他对诺贝尔和平奖的追求和国内制造业。这是他来华以来首次接受媒体提问。
特朗普在新闻讲话中宣布的一个重大变化是，他和习近平同意在人工智能领域建立“联合护栏”，这是特朗普的新举措，他一直坚称对该技术的监管将抑制美国的创新，并帮助中国在全球人工智能竞赛中处于领先地位。关于护栏是什么样子、何时谈判和发布以及如何在两国之间应用的更多细节尚未公布。
特朗普表示，习近平也喜欢他的术语“超级智能”，而不是人工智能，他说，“问题是，它可能太超级了。所以，习主席和我同意，我们将做一些联合护栏，我们两个。”
宣布未来的护栏之际，特朗普正面临美国日益严重的技术中断带来的阻力，最终导致特朗普更换了白宫网络主管。
特朗普在简报中补充说，他将继续推动在美国建设数据中心，此前两党中期选举选民都表示反对未来不受约束的增长。
在英伟达的影响下，特朗普前往亚洲会见习近平和普京
“让他们向你的社区付费，但要利用它们。不要让他们关闭，”特朗普在谈到因环境和噪音污染而引起社区批评的大型综合体时说道。
他还宣布对试图在美国境外建立数据中心的公司进行处罚。
“如果不是这个国家，外面还有其他人。我们不会允许我们的公司在我们国家之外建立数据中心。我们不会允许这种情况发生，”特朗普说。
特朗普的中国之行正值特朗普内阁讨论对华采取何种方针之际。特朗普商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克一直支持向中国出售美国芯片，英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋也持同样立场。财政部长斯科特·贝森特对中国表达了更为鹰派的观点，特朗普也承认了这两种观点。
随着卢特尼克和特朗普因与英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋的关系而面临强烈反对，这种分歧变得更加突出。黄仁勋在承认与一名可能是中国间谍的女性有染后辞职。
周五，特朗普表示，他只希望向中国出售“较旧的芯片”，而不是美国拥有的最尖端技术，他表示完全不向中国出售任何芯片都没关系，尽管他指出了这样做的缺点。
“你必须明白，中国也生产芯片，”特朗普说。 “如果我们不卖它们，他们就会自己生产。”

title_en: Man accused of sparking deadly Los Angeles wildfire found guilty
title_zh: 被控引发致命洛杉矶野火的男子被判有罪
summary: Verdict in case against former Uber driver Jonathan Rinderknecht comes after first trial ended with hung jury The 30-year-old accused of sparking the deadly Palisades fire in Los Angeles was found guilty of two federal arson charges in a Friday verdict that ca
summary_zh: 前 Uber 司机乔纳森·林德克内希特 (Jonathan Rinderknecht) 的案件在第一次审判以悬而未决的陪审团结束后作出判决。这位 30 岁的司机被指控引发了
body_en: Verdict in case against former Uber driver Jonathan Rinderknecht comes after first trial ended with hung jury

The 30-year-old accused of sparking the deadly Palisades fire in Los Angeles was found guilty of two federal arson charges in a Friday verdict that came months after his first trial concluded with a hung jury.
For two weeks, a fresh batch of jurors listened to prosecutors mount their case against Jonathan Rinderknecht.
They argued the former Uber driver was responsible for the January 2025 wildfire, which claimed 12 lives and devastated the Pacific Palisades, an affluent enclave on the California coast.

Rinderknecht, in prosecutors’ account, used a lighter to set a brush fire in the hillside area. The state cast him as a disgruntled young man who sought retribution against the world for personal gripes, including failed romances, and perceived societal injustices like wealth inequality.

Firefighters suppressed the so-called Lachman brush fire last January, but its embers simmered underground, before being swept by powerful winds and erupting above ground into the Palisades inferno that destroyed thousands of homes and businesses.
Rinderknecht had maintained his innocence, pleading not guilty to the revised charges of destruction of property by means of fire and arson affecting property used in interstate commerce.

For the retrial, jurors were instructed explicitly to not consider the adequacy of the fire department’s response to the Lachman and Palisades blaze. The department has faced criticism for failing to fully extinguish the Lachman fire that eventually reignited.

The note came after some of the first trial’s jurors were wary of pinning the blame squarely on Rinderknecht, citing the fire department’s past actions. Of that deadlocked panel, two voted for guilty, while 10 others were not convinced.
Rinderknecht’s defense team doubled down during the retrial on an alternative explanation for the Palisades fire, suggesting the initial brush blaze was ignited by fireworks.

Prosecutors dismissed the theory as “baseless” in a court filing where they raised concern over the reliability and late introduction of a defense witness, whose testimony would reference stains at a private residence that supposedly indicated fireworks had been discharged.
The state also presented digital evidence that cast doubt over Rinderknecht’s claim that he was at the bottom of a hiking trail when he saw the Lachman fire begin.
“These lies are telling – they are not mistakes,” prosecutor Danbee Kim reportedly said at trial. “Because he knows that where he was when the fire started was incriminating.”
Friday’s conviction followed two days of jury deliberation.
Standing outside a downtown Los Angeles courthouse on Friday, one juror cited the inconsistencies in Rinderknecht’s whereabouts during the fire as proof of his guilt.
“Logically, things started pointing towards him,” said Cameron, a 30-year-old college student who declined to give his last name to reporters .
Cameron stopped short of answering whether or not he believed Rinderknecht intended to burn down the Palisades.
He said he believed Rinderknecht’s “intent was to start a fire” and that his actions resulted in the devastating blaze.
The city and county of Los Angeles continue to face civil lawsuits from survivors of the fire and victims’ families.
body_zh: 对前 Uber 司机乔纳森·林德克内希特 (Jonathan Rinderknecht) 的案件的判决是在陪审团悬而未决的第一次审判结束后做出的
这名 30 岁的男子被指控在洛杉矶引发了致命的帕利塞兹火灾，在周五的一项判决中，他被判犯有两项联邦纵火罪，几个月前，他的第一次审判以陪审团悬而未决的方式结束。
两周以来，新一批陪审员听取了检察官针对乔纳森·林德克内西特提起的诉讼。
他们认为，前 Uber 司机应对 2025 年 1 月的山火负责，这场山火夺去了 12 人的生命，并摧毁了加利福尼亚海岸的一个富裕飞地太平洋帕利塞兹 (Pacific Palisades)。
根据检察官的说法，Rinderknecht 用打火机在山坡地区点燃了灌木丛。国家把他描绘成一个心怀不满的年轻人，他因个人不满而寻求对世界的报复，包括失败的恋情，以及认为财富不平等等社会不公正现象。
去年一月，消防队员扑灭了所谓的拉赫曼灌木丛火灾，但其余烬在地下沸腾，然后被强风席卷，在地面上喷发成栅栏地狱，摧毁了数千所房屋和企业。
林德克内西特坚称自己无罪，对修改后的通过放火和纵火破坏财产、影响州际贸易中使用的财产的指控不认罪。
在重审中，陪审员被明确指示不要考虑消防部门对拉赫曼和帕利塞德火灾的反应是否充分。该部门因未能完全扑灭最终重新燃起的拉赫曼大火而面临批评。
这份说明是在第一次审判的一些陪审员以消防部门过去的行为为由，对将责任直接归咎于林德克内西特持谨慎态度之后发出的。在这个陷入僵局的小组中，有两人投了有罪票，而另外 10 人则不相信。
林德克内西特的辩护团队在重审期间加倍努力，对帕利塞兹火灾提出了另一种解释，认为最初的灌木丛火灾是由烟花点燃的。
检察官在一份法庭文件中驳回了这一理论，称其“毫无根据”，他们对辩方证人的可靠性和迟到提出了担忧，该证人的证词提到了私人住宅上的污渍，据称这些污渍表明烟花已经燃放。
该州还提供了数字证据，对 Rinderknecht 的说法表示怀疑，即当他看到拉赫曼火灾时，他正在远足小道的底部。
据报道，检察官 Danbee Kim 在审判中表示：“这些谎言很能说明问题，它们并不是错误。” “因为他知道火灾发生时他所在的地方是有罪的。”
经过两天的陪审团审议后，周五被定罪。
周五，站在洛杉矶市中心法院外，一名陪审员援引林德克内西特在火灾期间行踪不一致的情况作为他有罪的证据。
“从逻辑上讲，事情开始朝着他的方向发展，”30 岁的大学生卡梅伦 (Cameron) 说道，他拒绝向记者透露自己的姓氏。
卡梅伦没有回答他是否相信林德克内西特打算烧毁栅栏。
他说，他相信林德克内西特的“意图是纵火”，他的行为导致了毁灭性的大火。
洛杉矶市和县继续面临火灾幸存者和受害者家属的民事诉讼。

title_en: Senate passes bipartisan energy bill amid environmental concerns
title_zh: 由于环境问题，参议院通过两党能源法案
summary: As Americans struggle with rising energy costs and increased demand driven by AI, the Senate passed a bipartisan bill that will speed up the approval process for data centers and power plants.
summary_zh: 随着美国人努力应对能源成本上涨和人工智能驱动的需求增加，参议院通过了一项两党法案，该法案将加快批准
body_en: Senate passes bipartisan energy bill amid environmental concerns As Americans struggle with rising energy costs and increased demand driven by AI, the Senate passed a bipartisan bill that will speed up the approval process for data centers and power plants.

NEW ALBANY, OHIO - NOVEMBER 1: In an aerial view, a portion of the Meta Prometheus Campus, an AI data center and supercluster project, is seen on November 1, 2026 in New Albany, Ohio. Jon Cherry/Getty Images hide caption

As Americans struggle with rising energy costs and increased demand driven by artificial intelligence, the Senate on Thursday passed a bipartisan bill that will speed up the approval process for data centers and power plants.
Experts say powering data centers uses more water than cooling them

The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act , passed 62-33. Fourteen Democrats and one Independent joined most Republicans in supporting the bill. It now heads to the House. The bill was authored by two Democrats and two Republicans.

"Tonight, the passage of permitting reform in the Senate finally became reality and we took a major step towards addressing the affordability concerns of the American people," said one of the bill's co-authors, West Virginia Republican Sen. Shelley Moore Capito.

Senate Majority Leader John Thune said the bill would "cut through decades of red tape" and "save the average household hundreds of dollars each year, and Americans will see better roads, more American manufacturing, and better-paying jobs."
Rhode Island Democratic Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse, who co-authored the bill, said "Americans will quickly begin getting some relief on their energy bills if the House follows suit."
AI data centers: How much are ratepayers on the hook for?
Nationwide, the cost of a kilowatt-hour has risen faster than overall inflation: more than 6% in the last year and 39% in the last five years .
Whitehouse also said the bill would make data centers pay for the power they use. There has been considerable pushback by the public against data centers in the U.S., cutting across party lines.

Some climate change advocates say the U.S. needs to speed up building renewable energy projects and transmission lines and argue that the bill will allow the country to build more solar, wind and battery projects.
But major environmental groups, including the Sierra Club and National Wildlife Federation , have opposed the bill, arguing it will weaken environmental accountability.

Many Democrats have also opposed the bill. They say it will worsen pollution by making it easier to greenlight oil and gas projects and energy-hungry data centers, while weakening protections for clean air and water.
The data center backlash is reshaping American politics — one community at a time
There is also concern the bill could undermine tribal rights.
"Don't sacrifice the Clean Water Act, hunting or fishing grounds, historic or sacred sites, or protections of tribal sovereignty," said Washington Democratic Sen. Maria Cantwell on X.

California Sen. Alex Padilla had similar concerns. "I support cutting red tape and getting more energy projects built, but not at the expense of tribal sovereignty and California's environment," he said .
body_zh: 由于环境问题，参议院通过了两党能源法案随着美国人努力应对能源成本上涨和人工智能驱动的需求增加，参议院通过了一项两党法案，该法案将加快数据中心和发电厂的审批流程。
俄亥俄州新奥尔巴尼 - 11 月 1 日：2026 年 11 月 1 日，在鸟瞰图中，可以看到俄亥俄州新奥尔巴尼的人工智能数据中心和超级集群项目 Meta Prometheus Campus 的一部分。乔恩·樱桃/盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
随着美国人努力应对能源成本上涨和人工智能驱动的需求增加，参议院周四通过了一项两党法案，该法案将加快数据中心和发电厂的审批流程。
专家表示，为数据中心供电比冷却数据中心消耗更多的水
两党以 62 票对 33 票通过《美国负担能力和就业法案》。十四名民主党人和一名独立人士与大多数共和党人一起支持该法案。现在它正前往众议院。该法案由两名民主党人和两名共和党人起草。
该法案的共同起草者之一、西弗吉尼亚州共和党参议员雪莱·摩尔·卡皮托表示：“今晚，参议院允许改革的通过终于成为现实，我们在解决美国人民的负担能力问题方面迈出了重要一步。”
参议院多数党领袖约翰·图恩表示，该法案将“消除数十年的繁文缛节”，“每年为普通家庭节省数百美元，美国人将看到更好的道路、更多的美国制造业和更高薪的工作。”
该法案的共同起草者、罗德岛州民主党参议员谢尔登·怀特豪斯表示，“如果众议院效仿，美国人将很快开始在能源账单上获得一些减免。”
人工智能数据中心：纳税人需要承担多少费用？
在全国范围内，每千瓦时的成本增长速度超过了总体通胀率：去年增长了 6% 以上，过去五年增长了 39%。
白宫还表示，该法案将使数据中心为其使用的电力付费。美国公众跨越党派界限，对数据中心提出了相当大的反对意见。
一些气候变化倡导者表示，美国需要加快建设可再生能源项目和输电线路，并认为该法案将允许该国建设更多太阳能、风能和电池项目。
但包括塞拉俱乐部和国家野生动物联合会在内的主要环保组织反对该法案，认为这将削弱环境责任。
许多民主党人也反对该法案。他们表示，这将使石油和天然气项目和高耗能数据中心更容易获得批准，同时削弱对清洁空气和水的保护，从而加剧污染。
数据中心的强烈反对正在重塑美国政治——一次一个社区
人们还担心该法案可能会损害部落权利。
华盛顿民主党参议员玛丽亚·坎特韦尔 (Maria Cantwell) 在 X 节目中表示：“不要牺牲《清洁水法》、狩猎或渔场、历史或圣地或对部落主权的保护。”
加州参议员亚历克斯·帕迪拉也有类似的担忧。 “我支持减少繁文缛节并建设更多能源项目，但不能以牺牲部落主权和加州的环境为代价，”他说。
